Living room furnished in parts/room-5.mjs: sofa on the north wall, two armchairs and a table facing the east hearth, bookshelves and a barrel on the west side, red carpet rug, one table pot and four hanging lanterns (one over the doorway lane).
./make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; this part places 24 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. `mcd room` says OK: 81/81 floor cells reachable, min light 8, no dark cells.
The hearth on the east wall is not in this copy's build (its part is a stub here), so the inside render shows no focal fireplace yet; the doorway lane (x10..17 z12, x17 z13..14) is kept clear for it.
left: Stair facing convention unverified: I used the toolkit's rule (facing = side of the full-height back) for the sofa and armchairs, so their seats face south and east. A render from the hearth's side should confirm they face the room.
Hearth (x18 z13..14, y14..16) is built by parts/hearth.mjs, which is a stub in this copy, so the focal fireplace does not appear in the render here; the room's lane is kept clear for it.
No plan.md checklist item or elements.md row maps to the living room, so none was ticked.

waste.what: Worked out the furniture cell by cell from the plan grid, then re-derived the grid's column offsets (x8 is the stair hall, x9 the partition with the doorway, x10..18 the floor) because the plan's 'o' marks the partition wall as furniture.
waste.cost: about 4 coordinate passes and one wrong reading of the x origin before the layout was right
waste.tool: `mcd plan` should print the floor's real x range and label wall-line cells as 'wall' rather than 'o', so the origin is unambiguous

waste.what: Checked the stair facing convention by reasoning only (the project docs disagree with vanilla as I remember it) and did not confirm it in a render.
waste.cost: no retries; left as an open check
waste.tool: a `mcd zoom` on one stair with its facing printed, or a stair-facing note in toolkit.md that says which side the seat faces

waste.what: Iterated the room check to remove two unreachable cells that were on top of a double bookshelf stack, a fix made by trial.
waste.tool: `mcd room` could name the cell's reason (top of a block the walker cannot climb) so the design fix is obvious

companions.task: confirm the spruce and oak stair facing on the sofa and armchairs so the seats face the room and the hearth, and check the stair well is left clear
build the east-wall hearth and its lane to the spec, so the focal piece exists when the room is merged
